why: Most of the builder brief describes the bar and allows the builder to run `npm ci && npm test` and write its own tests, which the criterion permits. But it ends with a "You are done when all of these hold:" block made of explicit PASS/FAIL conditions. These include "PASS when `printf '{"a":1}\n{bad\n' > /tmp/x.jsonl; node ... ` prints exactly `/tmp/x.jsonl:2: `... FAIL otherwise", "PASS when `node ... /nope; echo $?` prints 2", and a `grep -n jsonl-lint README.md` probe. The criterion forbids any PASS or FAIL condition in the builder brief. These probes also repeat checks in the verifier brief: item 1 checks a bad row with file:line output and exit 1, item 2 checks that a missing file exits 2, and item 5 checks that the root README lists the tool. So the builder is handed the checker's methods, and the criterion fails.
